objectClass.notes: A soft-vinyl toy of a low-poly game character, not a character render. Hard flat facets, visible edge creases, matte vinyl and zero smoothing groups are the identity. Ten separable parts with clean cylindrical/socketed joints.

reasoning: Deep hierarchy and a strict socket contract drive the tier, not surface detail.
Surface detail is deliberately low: the real object has no wear, dirt, scratches or relief.
The asymmetric arms mean the left and right chains cannot be mirrored, doubling the arm component count.

actionReadiness.contract: Every macro/meso component should be generated as a stable named Object3D pivot node with a mesh child, action metadata, optional sockets, collider proxy, and destruction metadata.
requiredComponentFields: attachment for child appendages, connectors, limbs, tubes, handles, legs, horns, wings, branches, or cables
authoringRules: Do not collapse independently movable parts into one mesh.
Put transforms on component pivot groups, not only on raw meshes.
For attached child parts, put the pivot at the semantic root/socket and build visible geometry from localStart to localEnd.
Represent hinge, socket, detachable, and breakable intent even when no animation is implemented yet.
Use simplified collider proxies for runtime physics instead of visual mesh colliders by default.

destructionPolicy.fractureGroupNaming: Use stable semantic names such as body-shell, left-hinge, glass-panel, branch-segment.
destructionPolicy.debrisStrategy: Prefer detachable component groups and a small number of procedural fragments over random mesh explosion.

assumptions: Total height is normalized to 1.000 from the sole plane to the tallest hair spike; the real figure's physical size is unknown and not needed.
The warm more-angle.webp white balance is treated as the true palette; the cooler product shots are recorded as the alternative reading.
The hair cap crown is placed at Y=0.905 where the dome meets the spike bases; that boundary is genuinely ambiguous and drives the head-unit figure.
The sole underside, the inner thigh faces above Y=0.269 and the top of the hair cap are not visible in any reference and are inferred.
Feet are mirrored; no reference view proves the two soles are identical, but nothing contradicts it.
The choker band is read from more-angle.webp only; the four orthographic shots do not resolve it.

referencePbr.hardLimit: The extracted albedo is the print itself. The height/normal channels are near-flat and that flatness is the finding: at 7x the eye edges are anti-aliased print lying on one unbroken facet, with no geometry crease under them. Build the face as a CanvasTexture or a de-lit projected crop, never as eye geometry.

repetitionSystems.name: Hair spike cluster
repetitionSystems.distribution: reference-copied asymmetric fan around the cap crown
repetitionSystems.placementRule: Place each spike from the observed reference layout: 1 dominant forward-leaning spike over the brow (sets Y=1.000), 2 large crown spikes fanning up-and-back, 2 lateral spikes projecting past the ears in front view, 2-3 short rear spikes visible only from the back, 1-2 short forward fringe wedges. Do NOT scatter procedurally and do NOT mirror - the fan is asymmetric.

performanceBudget.optimizationPolicy: The subject is genuinely low-poly. Keep the triangle count near the real object's facet count; adding geometry to smooth a facet is a fidelity regression, not polish.

lightingFromPhoto.observed: Highest value lands on the upward-facing facets (hair cap top, pauldron top face, sole top ledge), so the key sits high and slightly to the camera-left.
Shadow-side facets on the figure's right arm stay legible and read slightly cooler than the lit facets, so there is a soft cool fill opposite the key.
The near-black pauldron and fists keep a thin bright edge against the white background instead of merging into silhouette.
Seamless white sweep with a soft contact shadow under the soles; no coloured bounce and no visible reflection anywhere on the vinyl.
No specular hotspot appears on any surface under this lighting, which is what pins the material as matte soft vinyl rather than painted plastic.

The white sweep clips just short of pure white and the near-black pauldron keeps separation from the background, so the reference is close to a neutral exposure with a gentle filmic shoulder rather than a linear or clipped transfer.
lightingFromPhoto.intent: Render with ACESFilmic tone mapping at exposure 1.0. Raising exposure crushes the facet-to-facet value steps that carry the whole read on a flat-shaded subject; lowering it merges the two purples.

proceduralStrategy: Stage 1: build the ten parts in isolation, each at its own socket origin, no shared root.
Classify topology before picking a primitive for every component.
Block out the three hard silhouette gates before any detail work.
Attach children at sockets with the recorded overlap; never centre a child in space.
Keep flatShading on from the first pass - it is the identity, not a finishing step.
Stage 2 owns socket positions and pose rotations only; no geometry is authored there.
animationAnchors: each of the ten Stage 1 parts explodes along its socket axis and returns
fist-l/fist-r carry a 'grip' socket for a later weapon prop
destructionAnchors: actionProfile.destruction.fractureGroup marks detachable or breakable component sets
component seams and sockets define plausible break points instead of random explosions

risks.description: Mirroring the arms would put the pauldron and bracer on the wrong side.
risks.mitigation: Shoulders and forearms are authored as separate non-mirrored components and gated by featureReviewTarget handedness-asymmetry.

risks.description: The hip mass is the largest volume and the easiest to build as a cylinder or a skirt.
risks.mitigation: topologyClass and the kite localFeature pin the profile; gated at blockout.

risks.description: Smooth vertex normals would erase the identity of the subject.
risks.mitigation: flatShading is recorded per material and per component normalStrategy, and gated at material-pass.

risks.description: Procedurally scattering the spikes reads wrong immediately.
risks.mitigation: repetitionSystems.placementRule forbids scatter and mirroring; gated at form-refinement.

risks.description: The two photo sets disagree on white balance; picking the cool set collapses strap and belt into one colour.
risks.mitigation: Both readings are recorded on every material; the warm choice is stated in albedo.samplingNotes.

risks.description: analyze_texture.py calls six of the nine materials 'painted-metal' and would apply clearcoat 1.0, which would put a gloss lacquer on a matte vinyl toy.
risks.mitigation: Every material carries a finishClassification block recording the tool verdict, the applied matte finish, and why the tool was overridden. Gated by featureReviewTarget outfit-and-palette and by the faceted-shading feature group.

risks.description: The extracted PBR maps are near-flat and could be mistaken for missing evidence.
risks.mitigation: referencePbr.hardLimit records that the flatness is the finding, and normal.strength is deliberately 0.
